title: The SSF conformance PR added GET/PATCH/PUT stream handlers plus stream verify and status views without the add_stream provider permission check that the existing POST handler enforces, so any token holder for the app can read, modify, verify and disable its event streams.

findings.explanation: All database interactions use Django ORM methods (filter, first, save) with no string interpolation or raw SQL construction, eliminating the risk of SQL injection.

findings.explanation: The SSFStreamViewSet now inherits from GenericViewSet with Retrieve, Destroy, and List mixins but does not declare any permission or ownership checks. The queryset is `Stream.objects.all()`, potentially allowing any authenticated (or unauthenticated, depending on global settings) user to read, list, or delete streams belonging to other providers, which is an authorization flaw (missing access control).

evidence.content:
class SSFStreamViewSet(
    mixins.RetrieveModelMixin,
    mixins.DestroyModelMixin,
    mixins.ListModelMixin,
    GenericViewSet,
):
    """SSFStream Viewset"""

    queryset = Stream.objects.all()

findings.suggested_fix: Add appropriate permission classes (e.g., IsAuthenticated & custom object-level permission) and filter the queryset to only include streams the requesting user or client is authorized to access, such as `Stream.objects.filter(provider__owner=request.user)` or implement `get_queryset` with ownership checks.
